name: Mr. Backupsy
role: Looks after the backup — a bit nervous and anxious, so he checks everything three times
bubble.loading: One moment, I'm looking at the backup…
bubble.missing: I can't find the backup engine (unraid-backup), so there's nothing for me to do yet.
bubble.asleep: The engine's folder is on a sleeping disk — I don't dare wake it. Here's what I knew.
bubble.no_runs: There hasn't been a backup run yet. That makes me quite nervous.
bubble.running_kopia: I'm taking {share} offsite right now ({n} of {total}).
bubble.running_vm_shutdown: A backup is running — first I'm waiting for the VMs to shut down. The apps keep running meanwhile, nothing is stopped yet. I've asked nicely … and I'll ask again every minute!
bubble.running_check: I'm checking whether settings.ini still matches the server.
bubble.running_dryrun: I'm working out a dry run — nothing gets changed.
bubble.eta_rough: Done at about {time} — a rough guess: it's the first backup, there's nothing earlier to go by.
bubble.eta_late: It takes longer than usual — I expected it around {time}.
bubble.eta_partner_unknown: Done at about {time}, plus the step to the partner: it gets something for the first time, so I can't tell how long that takes yet.
bubble.first_eta: Oh dear — {share} goes offsite for the very first time ({size}). That takes many hours, it isn't stuck, I've checked three times! It's read at ~{rate}/s — it should be through at about {time}.
bubble.first_soon: Oh dear — {share} goes offsite for the very first time ({size}). Many hours — but now it's nearly through, any moment (read at ~{rate}/s). I'm watching!
bubble.first_measuring: Oh dear — {share} goes offsite for the very first time ({size}). That takes many hours, it isn't stuck! I'm still timing how fast it's read …
bubble.first_nosize: Oh dear — {share} goes offsite for the very first time. That takes many hours, it isn't stuck — how many, I can't say: I don't know how big it is.
bubble.first_sent: And only {sent} actually sent so far?! … No, no, that's right, I looked it up: Kopia compresses, and what the repository already has it doesn't send twice.
bubble.last_ok: Phew! The last backup {when} went through without problems.
bubble.last_ok_kopia: Phew! The last backup {when} went through: {ok} of {total} saved offsite.

bubble.last_warnings.one: The last backup {when} ended with one warning.
bubble.last_warnings.other: The last backup {when} ended with {warnings} warnings.

bubble.last_errors.other: Oh no — the last backup {when} had {errors} errors. Please have a look at the log.

bubble.last_failed: Oh no — the last backup {when} didn't finish.

bubble.old.one: That's more than a day ago.

bubble.no_schedule: Oh dear: no backup is scheduled! That makes me feel quite faint.

bubble.drift.other: {n} things on the server changed since the setup.

check.setup_how: Mr. Backupsy → «Set up…»: he reads the server and proposes everything.
check.engine_trust: The backup folder and its settings belong to root alone
check.engine_trust_how: Not so for {path}: the backup engine refuses to run until it is — it works as root and reads nothing others could have written. In a terminal on the server: {cmd}
check.schedule_how: Mr. Backupsy → Schedule: pick a time.
check.kopia_how: For the offsite copy: install Kopia from ⟦Apps⟧ (e.g. imagegenius/kopia), connect it to your repository once in the KopiaUI, then read the server again in Mr. Backupsy's «Set up…».
check.kopia_running_how: Start it on the Docker page.
check.kopia_autostart_how: It isn't on autostart: after a reboot or an array stop Kopia stays off, and the next backup goes without its offsite copy. On the Docker page switch on «⟦Autostart⟧» for «{name}» — for a container of a Compose stack, the stack's autostart in Compose Manager's list below the containers.
check.kopia_root_how: Set PUID and PGID to 0 in the template of «{name}» (now {puid}) — otherwise everything only its owner may read is missing from the backup.
check.kopia_mapping_how: In the template add a path: ⟦Host Path⟧ {path}, ⟦Container Path⟧ e.g. /uso, ⟦Access Mode⟧ «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧» (now: {now}). With plain «⟦Read Only⟧» Kopia sees empty folders. Kopia names its sources after the ⟦Container Path⟧ (/uso/<share>): changing it later makes new sources — in the same repository nothing is uploaded twice, but every file is read once more, and the old sources keep their history under the old names until you remove them in Kopia.
check.kopia_repo: Kopia is connected to its repository
check.kopia_repo_how: Connect the repository in the KopiaUI of «{name}», then click «Tour» at Mr. Backupsy.
check.kopia_emptied_how: The offsite copy is suddenly empty — snapshots on {when}: {before}, now: {now}, not deleted by the office. Possibly an attack or the wrong repository: since {since} nothing goes offsite (the local snapshots, packages and partners go on). If that wasn't you: delete nothing — Object Lock may still hold the data; the Consultant's Object Lock guide shows how to get it back through a second, read-only connection with --point-in-time. If the repository is really new, say so on Mr. Backupsy's page.
check.kopia_writes: The offsite storage takes what Kopia writes
check.kopia_writes_how: Since {since} the offsite storage ({storage}) has taken nothing from Kopia — reads may still answer, writes hang, nothing goes offsite. Look at the provider's status page and limits and whether the key may still write; then restart Kopia's container ({name}) — on Mr. Backupsy's page or under ⟦Docker⟧. Everything local goes on as usual.
check.kopia_lock_extend: Kopia extends the Object Lock of «{name}»
check.kopia_lock_extend_how: The repository has Object Lock ({mode}), but Kopia's full maintenance or its extending of the locks is switched off — once its retention period is over, whatever never changes loses its lock, and the protection against ransomware is gone without a word. In the console of the container «{name}»: kopia maintenance set --extend-object-locks=true --enable-full=true
check.kopia_lock_lapse: Kopia's Object Lock doesn't run out
check.kopia_lock_lapse_how: Kopia last extended the locks on {last} — they run out on {until}, then the repository is no longer protected against ransomware. Kopia extends them only at its full maintenance, and only the maintenance owner runs it: now {owner}, this office's Kopia is {me}. Keep the Kopia server in «{name}» running; if the owner isn't {me}, in its console: kopia maintenance set --owner=me — then once right away: kopia maintenance run --full
check.kopia_lock_late: Kopia's full maintenance runs on time
check.kopia_lock_late_how: Kopia's full maintenance is late (it last extended the locks on {last}, they hold until {until}). Only it extends the Object Lock — if it stays away, the locks run out. Maintenance owner: {owner}, this office's Kopia: {me}. Keep the Kopia server in «{name}» running; if the owner isn't {me}, in its console: kopia maintenance set --owner=me
check.kopia_lock_never: Kopia has extended the Object Lock at least once
check.kopia_lock_never_how: Kopia has never extended the locks yet — its first full maintenance was due on {next} and hasn't run. Only it extends the Object Lock; without it the locks run out at the end of their retention period. Maintenance owner: {owner}, this office's Kopia: {me}. Keep the Kopia server in «{name}» running; if the owner isn't {me}, in its console: kopia maintenance set --owner=me

setup.applied_errors: Applied with errors — settings.ini is written, but not everything was done; see the messages.
setup.apply_kopia_stuck: The offsite storage has taken nothing since {since}, so only a later Apply sets Kopia's policies. Everything else is applied now.

setup.forget_warn: Until you apply again, no backup runs — not on schedule either.
setup.forget_keeps: What is backed up stays: local snapshots, dumps and archives, what lies offsite (Kopia's snapshots and policies), the history. The old settings are then in state/reset-<time>/.
setup.forget_default: Your default for new things («{name}») goes too — the setup starts with my proposals again.
setup.forget_snapshots: Snapshots of shares you no longer back up afterwards stay where they are — you can clear them away at Ms. Snapshotini's.
setup.bubble_forgetting: I'm putting the old settings aside — then I start anew.
setup.forgotten: Forgotten — I'm looking at the server anew.
setup.forget_failed: Forgetting didn't work — see the messages below.
setup.apply_none: Nothing changed — applying writes the same settings again and lines up Kopia's policies.
setup.apply_new: Nothing is set up yet. This is how I set myself up:
setup.apply_hint: Mr. Backupsy checks everything again, keeps the previous settings.ini, writes the new one and — if backups go offsite — lines up Kopia's policies. The schedule stays as it is.
setup.apply_hint_new: Mr. Backupsy checks everything again, writes settings.ini and — if backups go offsite — Kopia's policies. No backup starts.
setup.apply_responsibility: After the first runs, check that everything you need is in the backup, and try a restore now and then. A backup can be faulty or incomplete, and your data stays your responsibility.
setup.proposal_tip: A proposal of Mr. Backupsy's — you didn't change anything here.

setup.declined.other: {n} proposals you declined — I don't make them again while they stay the same:

setup.filter.none: Nothing in this step fits the filter.

setup.key_unknown: the entry «{key}», which Mr. Backupsy doesn't know, goes
setup.key_unknown_tip: Written into settings.ini by hand. Apply writes the settings anew with what Mr. Backupsy knows — this line is not kept.

setup.key.general_view_root: Where btrfs snapshots can be browsed
setup.key.general_min_free_gb: Free space kept in the backup place (GB)
setup.kopia_sub: Where the backups go, the flash, and whether they also go offsite (encrypted with Kopia: S3, Backblaze B2, SFTP, WebDAV, a NAS …). Local only doesn't help against fire, theft or a dead server.
setup.kopia_on_hint: Encrypted with Kopia: S3, Backblaze B2, SFTP, WebDAV, a NAS … You connect Kopia to that storage once in the KopiaUI — passwords and keys never go into these settings.
setup.kopia_recheck: Offsite was off so far, so I haven't checked Kopia yet. Apply, then read again — then I check the container, the mapping and the repository.
setup.k_probe_0: Kopia sees new snapshot mounts right away
setup.k_probe_1: Kopia does NOT see new snapshot mounts
setup.k_caretaker: The team lead explains what to do.
setup.k_hostid: Kopia's host name is a container ID — after re-creating «{name}» all sources would look new. Set a fixed host name in the KopiaUI.
setup.k_problem.no_container: There is no Kopia container for the offsite copy. Install one from ⟦Apps⟧ (e.g. imagegenius/kopia) and connect it to your storage in the KopiaUI.
setup.k_problem.container_gone: Kopia's container {name} is gone. Make it anew from its template (⟦Docker⟧ → ⟦Add Container⟧, template {name}) — until then nothing goes offsite.
setup.k_problem.docker_off: Docker is switched off — the offsite copy needs it, because Kopia runs in a container. You can switch Docker on under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Docker⟧.
setup.k_problem.not_running: «{name}» is not running — start it on the Docker page.
setup.k_problem.no_mapping: «{name}» has no mapping for {root}. Add the path {root} → {root} with ⟦Access Mode⟧ «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧».
setup.k_problem.propagation: The mapping of {root} in «{name}» doesn't pass on what is mounted below it — Kopia would see empty folders. Set ⟦Access Mode⟧ «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧».
setup.k_problem.probe: «{name}» doesn't see new mounts under {root}. Re-create the container after changing the template.
setup.k_problem.no_repo: «{name}» isn't connected to a repository yet. Connect it once in the KopiaUI, then read again.
setup.k_problem.not_root: «{name}» doesn't run as root — set PUID and PGID to 0 in its template, otherwise files only their owners may read are missing.
setup.shares_sub: What steps 1 and 2 decide is greyed out. You decide the rest here. Big shares are proposed as "not backed up"; a new setup sends nothing offsite on its own — you pick what goes there.
setup.why.system: Docker image and libvirt.img — Unraid pulls the containers again, the run saves the VM configuration separately; no snapshot needed
setup.why.domains: VM disks — inconsistent while VMs run; back VMs up separately
setup.why.domains_snap: VM disks — local snapshot; how each VM is held for it, you set below under VMs
setup.why.timemachine: Time Machine target ({arg}) — holds other computers' backups
setup.why.timemachine_name: probably a Time Machine target (going by the name) — would hold other computers' backups
setup.why.kopia_workdir: Kopia's own config, cache or repository
setup.why.big_container: container data, big ({size}) — leave out the big folders in the details
setup.why.size_unknown: size unknown — measure or decide on purpose
setup.why.no_snapshots: no snapshot possible here (e.g. XFS) — Kopia (offsite) reads it live, or leave it out
setup.why.gone: doesn't exist any more — entry will be removed
setup.f_retention_hint: Empty = like all shares. Example: «7 0 0» keeps a week; the long history then comes from the offsite copy.
setup.f_kopia_retention: Kopia keeps (latest hourly daily weekly monthly annual)
setup.f_kopia_retention_hint: Six numbers or «inherit»; empty = like all shares.
setup.f_ignore: Kopia leaves out (one rule per line, relative to the share)
setup.f_folders: Folders in this share (with the containers that use them) — click to have Kopia leave one out or take it back:
setup.f_folders_none: No folders to click here — rules go into the field “Kopia leaves out”.
setup.f_folders_many: Too many folders to list them all — write rules into the field “Kopia leaves out”.
setup.f_folders_asleep: Not looked at on {disks}: asleep, I did not wake it — folders only there are missing here.
setup.f_folder_on: left out — click to back it up again
setup.f_folder_off: backed up — click to leave it out
setup.f_method_hint: auto = from a snapshot; live = read the running share (only if snapshots aren't possible).
setup.f_children_hint: Unticked datasets are neither snapshotted nor backed up.
setup.containers_sub: For the seconds of the snapshots, containers that write into backed-up shares are stopped — then the snapshot is clean, not just crash-consistent.
setup.ct_kopia: always keeps running · never backed up itself
setup.app_kopia_text: You don't need Kopia's folders for a restore, only: 1. Its template – it is backed up with the flash; the consultant shows how to set it up anew («Install by hand»). 2. Your access data: repository password, storage keys, KopiaUI login. Keep them apart from the server, or you can't reach your backups.
setup.ct_risk_hint: This container writes into backed-up data; if it keeps running, its snapshot is like pulling the plug. Apps with their own SQLite database (Emby, Jellyfin, Plex, *arr …) are only clean when stopped.

setup.ct_volumes_cache_hint: These Docker volumes only hold a cache (downloaded models, thumbnails, temporary files). They are not in the backup — that is fine: after a restore the app fetches their contents again by itself.

help.run: A backup run, step by step
help.run_text: Every run goes through these steps: look around, database dumps, shut down VMs, stop apps, snapshots (a few minutes of standstill), offsite copy, tidy up. The bracket under the steps shows when apps and VMs are stopped. «Done at about» comes from earlier runs; for a source's first upload, from its size and the reading speed.
help.results_text: How a run ended. «not finished»: it broke off unexpectedly, for example through a restart. «stopped»: you stopped it, or with «array stop» it ended on purpose – nothing is lost. «skipped»: it didn't start because the engine was busy; it changed nothing. The log has the details.
help.protection_text: Every share and how the backup protects it. The labels are the same everywhere in the office:
help.buttons_text: The tour compares server and settings and changes nothing. Back up now: a full run, one without the offsite upload, or a dry run. Stop ends it cleanly, containers come back.
help.setup: I read the server and show proposals with reasons. You change what you like and apply. It all happens in the browser.
help.history: The last runs with their result. You see how much went offsite and how long containers were stopped. A click on a run opens its log.
help.drift: New shares or containers since the setup, or settings that don't fit any more. «Set up…» takes them over.
help.restore: Where the local snapshots, the offsite copy (Kopia) and the packages are. Bringing things back is Mr. Restori's job. He does it per app and VM, with ready-made commands.
disclaimer: No backup is a guarantee – it can be faulty or incomplete. You are responsible for your data: test a restore now and then, and keep several copies, one offsite.
help.draft_text: Everything here is a draft until you press Apply at the bottom. Discard goes back to what was read. If there are only my proposals, Discard sets them aside until I read the server again.
help.replan: I read the server again: shares, containers, databases and Kopia. Nothing changes.
help.reasons_text: Every proposal says why: as before, new, too big, Time Machine target, Kopia's own folder …
help.details: Per share: the local and the Kopia retention, the method and the child datasets. Also the folders Kopia leaves out; the share's folders are one click away.
help.apply: First you see every change. Then I check again, keep the previous settings.ini, write the new one and line up Kopia.
help.forget: Puts your settings and the default aside and starts the assistant as on a new server. Nothing backed up is deleted. No backup runs until you apply again. The button is at the top right.
schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.intro: Unraid starts the run on this schedule itself, even when the office isn't open – while the array runs. Pick a quiet time: containers pause briefly for the snapshots.
schedule.custom_hint: Five fields as in User Scripts "Custom", e.g. 0 3 * * 1-6 (Monday to Saturday at 3 am).
schedule.examples_tip:
15 * * * * — every hour at quarter past
0 * * * * — every hour on the hour
0 */6 * * * — every 6 hours (0, 6, 12 and 18 o'clock)
0 1,12 * * * — every day at 1 am and at noon
0 3 * * 1-6 — Monday to Saturday at 3 am
If a backup is still running, the next one is skipped — with a notification.
schedule.off_hint: The backup then only runs when you start it here.
schedule.duration: A run took about {duration} lately — done around {end}.
schedule.order_hint: Same minute as Ms. Moverelli's run — whoever starts first runs to the end, the other waits. Better give one of them another time.
order.waited_night: waited {min} min for Ms. Moverelli's run
errors.backup_night_running: Ms. Moverelli's run is going right now — start the backup once it is done (a scheduled backup waits for it by itself).
errors.backup_same_minute: Ms. Moverelli's run starts at {time} too — please pick another minute: the two never start together.
schedule.not_live: Saved, but Unraid didn't take it into the crontab yet — reinstalling the plugin under ⟦Plugins⟧ puts it in.
schedule.after_setup: Only the schedule is missing now.
greet.2: Wait, where did I put … ah, there.
greet.3: I do hope the power stays on today…
greet.4: I checked three times. Better safe than sorry.
greet.5: Is the array still there? … Phew.
greet.6: Backups can go wrong, you know — I check everything three times, but please test a restore now and then. In the end your data is your responsibility …
greet.7: One copy is no copy! Three copies, two kinds of storage, one far away — 3-2-1. Only then do I sleep well.
fit.yes: Mr. Backupsy is coming — he only asked three times whether Kopia ("{kopia}") is really there.
fit.no_kopia: Mr. Backupsy would come, but he's nervous: without Kopia he can't save anything offsite. You can install Kopia later — I'll tell you how.
fit.no_cow: Mr. Backupsy declined: without ZFS or btrfs he can't take snapshots. "That makes me dizzy", he said.
fire_note: The scheduled backup keeps running as long as its schedule is on. If it should stop, switch it off first under his "Schedule…".

setup.pending_title: New compared with the saved settings
setup.bubble_old: This is what I knew {when} — things may have changed since. Click «Plan anew» before you apply.
check.nextcloud_datadir: Nextcloud "{name}": data folder readable by Nextcloud only
check.nextcloud_datadir_how: {path} is set to {mode} — Nextcloud then refuses to work, and maintenance mode for the backup can't be switched on. Unraid resets a share's root to 0777 nobody:users when share settings are saved unless the root belongs to the group «users». Lasting fix: chown 33:100 and chmod 0750 on {path} (www-data:users — Nextcloud is content, Unraid leaves it alone), e.g. as a User Script.
paused.note: Only for the dumps and snapshots — then I start everything again, I promise. Even after a crash: it's noted down here.
message.nc_datadir_readable: Nextcloud refused maintenance mode: its data folder is readable by others. How to fix it: 1. chown 33:100 and chmod 0750 on the data folder. 2. Start the run again.
message.nc_maintenance_failed: Nextcloud didn't go into maintenance mode — the log has occ's message. Look at Nextcloud's own page, then start the run again.
setup.ds_label: Backup place (the packages of apps and VMs)
setup.ds_missing: Required: without a backup share of its own I back up nothing. Backups don't belong in appdata.
setup.ds_off: "{share}" isn't backed up itself (not backed up) — the packages would keep no history and be safe nowhere. Set the share above to snapshot or snapshot + offsite.
setup.ds_local: "{share}" doesn't go offsite — the packages would stay on this server only. Better set the share above to "Snapshot + offsite".
check.dumps_share: A backup place of its own is set
check.dumps_share_how: Create the share «UnraidSecretaryOffice» (not on the pool of appdata, SMB export off), then Mr. Backupsy → «Set up…» → Basics → Backup place. Any other share of its own works too. Without one he refuses every run — backups don't belong in appdata.
check.dumps_offsite_how: "{share}" is set to "{mode}" — dumps and archives stay on this server only. At Mr. Backupsy, "Set up…", set the share to "Snapshot + offsite".
check.app_share: Every app's data share is backed up as far as its app
check.app_share_how: An app that writes into a share of its own (S3 buckets, cloud files, Time Machine) is backed up no further than that share — otherwise a restore brings the app back without its data.
check.app_share_link: To the shares in the setup
check.app_share_kopia: The apps' data shares go offsite like the apps

check.app_share_kopia_how.one: {apps}: the app goes offsite, the share in brackets stays on this server — restored elsewhere, the app comes back without its data. If it should go too: at Mr. Backupsy, «Set up…», set the share to «Snapshot + offsite».
check.app_share_kopia_how.other: {apps}: the apps go offsite, the shares in brackets stay on this server — restored elsewhere, the apps come back without their data. If they should go too: at Mr. Backupsy, «Set up…», set the shares to «Snapshot + offsite».

check.app_share_kopia_link: To the shares in the setup
check.app_share_partner: The apps' data shares go to the partner {partner} like the apps

check.app_share_partner_how.one: {apps}: the app goes to the partner {partner}, the share in brackets doesn't — restored there, the app comes back without its data. If it should go too: at Mr. Backupsy, «Set up…», give the share the partner {partner}.
check.app_share_partner_how.other: {apps}: the apps go to the partner {partner}, the shares in brackets don't — restored there, the apps come back without their data. If they should go too: at Mr. Backupsy, «Set up…», give the shares the partner {partner}.

check.app_share_partner_link: To the shares in the setup
check.app_share_off: The apps' data shares are backed up

check.app_share_off_how.one: {apps}: the app is backed up, the share in brackets isn't backed up at all — a restore brings the app back without its data. At Mr. Backupsy, «Set up…», choose how the share is backed up.
check.app_share_off_how.other: {apps}: the apps are backed up, the shares in brackets aren't backed up at all — a restore brings the apps back without their data. At Mr. Backupsy, «Set up…», choose how the shares are backed up.

check.app_share_off_link: To the shares in the setup
message.dumps_missing: No backup place set — dumps and archives need a backup share of their own; they don't belong in appdata. Choose one in "Set up…".
message.dumps_unknown: The backup place doesn't exist as a share (any more). Choose another one in "Set up…".
message.dumps_forbidden: The backup place is in appdata, system or domains — backups don't belong there. Choose a share of its own in "Set up…".
message.dumps_off: The backup place isn't backed up itself — the dumps would be safe nowhere. Let the share be backed up in "Set up…".
message.docker_silent: Docker is switched on but doesn't answer — the run ended before it stopped anything; nothing was backed up. Restart Docker under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Docker⟧, then start the run again.
message.no_space_packages: Not enough free space in the backup place {place}: {free} free, at least {need} should stay free. Nothing was backed up. Make room there or lower «Free space kept in the backup place» in «Set up…», and start again.
message.no_space_packages_plain: Not enough free space in the backup place. Nothing was backed up. Make room there or lower «Free space kept in the backup place» in «Set up…», and start again.
help.rules_text: A click on a share shows its rules: what Kopia leaves out, how long it keeps versions, what stays on this server and whether Kopia is really set up like that. Change them only here, not in the KopiaUI – changes there I report as drift, and the next Apply sets them back.
policy.ok: Kopia is set up exactly like this.
policy.differs: Kopia's settings for this share differ from the ones here — Apply in «Set up…» lines them up again.
policy.skipped: Kopia lacks a rule of this share, so the run leaves it out. Apply in «Set up…» fixes it.
policy.unknown: Not compared yet — the next tour or run does it (needs Kopia running and unraid-backup 2.14 or newer).
policy.root_differs: The settings every share inherits differ in Kopia, too:
pd.where_to_change: Rules and retention are set here, not in the KopiaUI.
local.none: no local snapshot (the file system can't do it)
diff.schedule: Kopia may start these sources on its own schedule (here: only during the run)
diff.one_file_system: one-file-system is {have} in Kopia (needed: false, so child datasets come along)
check.mnt_folders: Nothing of the office directly in /mnt
check.mnt_folders_how: Fix Common Problems rightly reports {folders}. The snapshots belong under /mnt/addons (Unraid's place for that, in RAM, no data of its own): in the template of «{name}» change only the ⟦Host Path⟧ of the snapshot mapping to {path} (⟦Container Path⟧ and «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧» stay), then Mr. Backupsy → «Set up…» → Apply. The next run removes the old folders.
schedule.no_settings: First I need to be set up: "Set up…" → Apply. Then you can pick a time here.
help.vms_text: A VM's disks are in the snapshot of its share. In «Set up…» → VMs you choose what a running VM goes through: «freeze» (best, with the guest agent), «pause» for seconds, «shut down» (takes minutes) or «keep running» (only crash-consistent). A VM with its own dataset can be left out or keep its snapshots for a different time. With a partner, «local + partner» sends that dataset to the partner after every run; grey means the VM shares its dataset.
setup.vms_sub: Which VM do you need back when a disk dies? VMs that are backed up are paused or frozen for the seconds of the snapshot; their share gets a snapshot for it.
setup.apps_sub: A compose stack is one app. Apps that are backed up stop together for a moment for the snapshot, their databases are dumped first. Further shares of an app you tick yourself — they can grow fast.
setup.apps_docker_off: Docker is switched off — no apps to back up.
setup.apps_gone: Gone — in the settings, no longer on the server
setup.app_gone_had: It went offsite as a source of its own: {list}
setup.app_dump_hint: Before the snapshot the database is dumped and checked right away — part of the app when it is backed up.
setup.app_nodata_hint: This app binds no folder in a share. Its template or compose file goes into its package in the backup place with every backup.
setup.app_nodata_noflash: This app binds no folder in a share — only its template or compose file on the flash would be backed up. But the flash is not backed up.
setup.app_hold_hint: Stop: the app pauses a few seconds and closes its files cleanly – the safest. Keep running: the snapshot catches its files mid-work; at worst the last seconds are missing. Good for media servers and apps with few changes.
setup.app_dep_hint: the whole share is backed up, like the app
setup.app_dep_same: {share} is already backed up like the app — nothing to change.
setup.app_dep_cannot: {share} can't go to a partner: {why}. It is backed up already — «{mode}»; ticking it here would change nothing.
setup.app_dep_kept: {share} stays at «{mode}» in step 3 — change it there.
setup.app_dep_step3_hint: You chose this share in step 3 already. Ticking it ties it to the app: it then follows the app's choice.
setup.level_hint.0: Not backed up: keeps running, no dump, no package, nothing goes offsite.
setup.level_hint.1: Local snapshot; databases dumped first; its template or compose file goes into its package in the backup place.
setup.level_hint.2: Like local, and offsite too — as a Kopia source of its own, with its own retention (step 4).
setup.level_hint.partner: Like local, and after every backup its ZFS snapshot goes encrypted to the partner office ({partners}), only the changed blocks. The partner keeps it with its own retention.
setup.level_hint.partner_kopia: Like local, to the partner office ({partners}) and offsite as a Kopia source of its own — both.
setup.lock_hint: The VMs and apps above decide this. Change it there.
setup.lock_pkg: offsite — templates, dumps and VM configuration belong with what goes there
setup.ds_kopia: goes offsite too, because something is backed up there
setup.retention_sub: Two rows of numbers: how long local snapshots stay and how long Kopia keeps the offsite states. Dumps and configurations live inside those snapshots.
setup.r_kopia_hint: Latest, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, annual states. "inherit" = like Kopia's global policy.
setup.r_exceptions: Exceptions: per share in its details (step 3), per VM with a dataset of its own in step 1, offsite per app and VM right above.
setup.vm_service_off: The VM service is off — nothing to set up.
setup.vm_agent_hint.yes: qemu-guest-agent runs inside the VM: it can flush and freeze the VM's file systems for the snapshot.
setup.vm_agent_hint.no: The VM runs, but no guest agent answers. Freezing needs qemu-guest-agent inside the VM (for Windows: the virtio-win guest tools); until then pause is the safe choice.
setup.vm_agent_hint.channel: The VM is off, but a guest agent channel is configured — freezing should work when it runs.
setup.vm_agent_hint.none: No guest agent channel is configured for this VM.
setup.vm_tpm_hint: The VM has a virtual TPM. Its state is in the VM configuration archive next to the dumps.
setup.vm_gpu_hint: Passed-through hardware (e.g. a GPU). On another server its addresses differ — the VM's XML has to be adjusted there.
setup.vm_cannot_hint: No snapshot holds this disk, so the backup doesn't contain it.
setup.vm_shared_hint: Its disks lie in a dataset together with the share or other VMs: it always goes with the share's snapshot and can't be left out or kept apart on its own.
setup.vm_upload_hint: A VM's first upload offsite reads its disks whole, empty parts as zeros: {size}, though only {used} is used. This happens once; later runs skip what didn't change. Local snapshots don't mind.
setup.vm_share_off_hint: The share holding its disks is set to off — so the VM isn't backed up either.
setup.vm_prep_hint: Freeze: the guest agent writes everything out and freezes the file systems for a moment (seconds). Pause: the VM stands still for the seconds of the snapshot. Shut down: cleanly before, started again after (minutes; never switched off hard).
setup.vm_ret_hint: How long this VM's snapshots stay: daily weekly monthly, e.g. 3 1 0 = three days, one week, no month. Empty = like the share “{share}” (the numbers in the field).
setup.vm_noagent_hint: Freezing needs the guest agent inside the VM. Without it the run pauses the VM instead.
vm.prep_text.freeze: Its guest agent flushes and freezes the file systems for the seconds of the snapshot; the VM keeps running.
vm.prep_text.pause: The VM stops for the seconds of the snapshot and then runs on — like pulling the plug, but no write is cut in half.
vm.prep_text.shutdown: Shut down cleanly before anything else and started again after the snapshot. If it doesn't shut down in 5 minutes, it is paused instead – never forced off.
vm.prep_text.none: It keeps running: its disks in the snapshot are only crash-consistent, as after a power cut.
vm.not_set_up_hint: Its disks are in the share's snapshot, but nobody told Mr. Backupsy how to treat it — it keeps running (crash-consistent). «Set up…» → VMs.
vm.done_text.not_running: was off — the snapshot is clean
vm.done_text.failed: could not be held — kept running
vm.left_out: Left out: its dataset is not snapshotted.
vm.keeps_shared: like its share (it shares a dataset)
vm.note_tpm: Virtual TPM: its state is in the VM configuration archive.

vm.note_gpu.one: 1 device passed through — on another server the VM's XML needs adjusting.
vm.note_gpu.other: {n} devices passed through — on another server the VM's XML needs adjusting.

stat.docker_silent: Docker is switched on but doesn't answer
help.packages_text: Every run writes a small package per app and VM to the backup place: an app's templates or compose files and dumps, a VM's XML, UEFI variables and TPM state. The data itself is in the snapshots. «Stale» means the app or VM is gone or no longer backed up. The package is never deleted.

stat.pk_old.one: 1 old run folder — goes once a run packed everything
stat.pk_old.other: {n} old run folders — go once a run packed everything

stat.pk_asleep: its disk sleeps — as last seen
stat.pk_first: the next run writes them and clears the old run folders away
drift_code.place_no_history: The backup place «{share}» has no snapshots, so the packages keep no history. Better: a share on a ZFS or btrfs pool.
drift_code.place_not_kopia: The backup place «{share}» doesn't go offsite — the packages (templates, dumps, VM configurations) stay on this server only.
pk.group_hint: Each app's templates or compose files and dumps, in {path}, protected like the backup place. The apps' data lies in their shares.
pk.found_unset: My settings are gone — I found these packages without them, in {path}. I only show them until I'm set up again («Set up…»); Mr. Restori can bring them back already.
pk.kept_hint: This run couldn't dump it (failed, or the container wasn't running) — the last good dump stays in the package, from the run shown.
pk.stale_hint: Written by an earlier run ({when}): the app or VM is gone or no longer backed up. The package stays — it is never deleted.
pk.gone_hint.app: {name} no longer exists on this server — no container, no image. Its package can go into Ms. Dustdevil's storeroom (above the table).

pk.gone_intro.one: A package in the backup place belongs to something that no longer exists — Mr. Restori's drill can't practise with it:
pk.gone_intro.other: {n} packages in the backup place belong to things that no longer exist — Mr. Restori's drill can't practise with them:

pk.gone_line.app: Package of {name}: the app no longer exists
pk.gone_line.vm: Package of {name}: the VM no longer exists
pk.gone_aside_tip: Moves the package into Ms. Dustdevil's storeroom — put back or emptied there, never deleted at once.
pk.gone_text.app: {name} no longer exists on this server: no container and no image of it. Its package goes into Ms. Dustdevil's storeroom, on the same disk inside the share:
pk.gone_text.vm: {name} is no longer a VM on this server. Its package goes into Ms. Dustdevil's storeroom, on the same disk inside the share:
pk.gone_back: Nothing is deleted. Ms. Dustdevil lists it under «Tidying up»: put back with a click, or emptied when you want. Mr. Restori's drill no longer lists it.
pk.moved_hint: Its app is now backed up as {other} — the old package can go into Ms. Dustdevil's storeroom (above the table).

pk.moved_intro.one: A stale package in the backup place belongs to an app that is now backed up under another name:
pk.moved_intro.other: {n} stale packages in the backup place belong to apps that are now backed up under another name:

pk.moved_line.containers: Package of {name}: its containers are now backed up as {other} (same containers) — the old package can go into the storeroom
pk.moved_line.folders: Package of {name}: its folder is now backed up as {other} (same folder) — the old package can go into the storeroom
pk.moved_text: The package of {name} is stale: the same app is now backed up as {other} ({signal}). The old package goes into Ms. Dustdevil's storeroom, on the same disk inside the share:
pk.errors_hint: Part of it failed in the last run (see the log) — what failed was kept from the run before.
pk.warnings_hint: The last run packed it with a warning (e.g. a database container wasn't running) — see the log.
pk.ok_hint: Written completely by the last run.
pk.d_images_hint: manifest.json in the package records each container's image with its digest and its docker inspect.
pk.d_restore: Mr. Restori brings it back — his desk shows how, per app and VM.
pk.vm_left_out: none — the VM is left out
pk.vm_none: none yet — the next run writes it
restore.pk_text: In {path}: apps/<app>/ (templates, compose files, dumps), vms/<vm>/ (XML, UEFI variables, TPM), server/ (share settings, libvirt.img) and flash/. Older states are in that share's snapshots, or offsite.
setup.lock_place: the backup place — its snapshots keep the packages' history
setup.lock_place_hint: The packages keep their history in this share's snapshots: at least a local snapshot. Offsite on top is your choice.
setup.place_secondary: Secondary storage set ({where}) — the mover would move the packages between drives. Better one place only: no secondary storage.
setup.place_why.same_pool: on the same pool as appdata ({where})
setup.place_why.no_history: without snapshots ({where}: only the newest state, no earlier ones)
setup.place_why.no_snapshots: without snapshots (only the newest state, no earlier ones)
setup.place_risk.same_pool: If this pool fails, apps and backup are gone together.
setup.place_risk.no_redundancy: If its drive fails, the backup is gone.
setup.place_help: What helps: switch on offsite, connect a partner or choose another pool.
setup.place_local_only: Only local — the packages stay on this server alone; offsite or a partner would keep a copy elsewhere.
setup.place_info_kopia: Just so you know — a copy goes offsite:
setup.place_info_partner: Just so you know — a copy goes to the partner {partner}:
setup.place_title: What matters for the backup place
setup.place_1: Not on the pool appdata lies on — a failing pool would take the apps and their dumps together.
setup.place_2: Best an exclusive share on a ZFS pool: only then do my packages keep earlier backups in snapshots, and only then may the place go to a partner office. A btrfs pool does for snapshots, never for a partner.
setup.place_3: Redundant if possible: a mirror pool. The array only as a last resort – there's no snapshot of the whole share, no partner, and on XFS only the last state.
setup.place_4: One place only: no secondary storage, no mover — the packages shouldn't wander between drives.
setup.place_5: It stays small, often under a gigabyte: configurations, dumps, the flash archive. The big data stays in its own shares, so a small disk will do. If it grows a lot, something is off, a huge dump, say.
setup.place_name: Name suggestion: {name} — on a ZFS pool, exclusive, not on the array
setup.place_back: Once it exists, come back here: when the setup opens I look at the server again by myself (or click «Plan anew»).
setup.bubble_place: Oh dear, there's no share for my packages yet, and without one I back up nothing at all! Right below you have Unraid create it with one click — you see where it goes first.
setup.bubble_place_choose: Oh dear, I don't know yet which share becomes my backup place, so I back up nothing at all! Right below you have Unraid create one — or you take one that's there.
setup.why.backup_place: the backup place — its snapshots keep the packages' history
setup.ch_share_gone_why: removed — the share doesn't exist any more
setup.ch_share_renamed: removed — the share is now called «{name}», its settings go with it
setup.data_off: {what} lie in {path} — and that share isn't backed up. After a restore the database and the files won't match. Back up {share} too: tick it above, or choose it in step 3.
setup.data_local: {what} lie in {path}. That share stays local while the app goes offsite – after losing the server, database and files won't match. Send {share} offsite as well.
setup.items_sub: Each app and VM at «local + offsite» is a Kopia source of its own (.apps/<name> or .vms/<name>) with its own retention; empty = as above. The shares leave these folders out, so nothing goes up twice.
setup.item_pkg_only: only its package (no folder of its own)
setup.offers: Kopia may leave out — the app rebuilds these itself:
setup.offer_on: Left out of Kopia — a click takes it along again.
setup.offer_off: Goes offsite — a click leaves it out.
setup.offer_hint.cache: The app rebuilds it by itself; the local snapshots keep it anyway.
setup.offer_hint.immich: Immich can rebuild it from the originals — but for a big library that takes hours (Administration → Jobs). The local snapshots keep it anyway.
setup.item_ret_hint: Six numbers: latest hourly daily weekly monthly annual, e.g. 7 0 14 8 24 5 — «inherit» for one of them takes the number above. Empty = like everything else.
setup.item_ignore_hint: One rule per line, relative to its source — there every part lies where it lies on the server, e.g. {example}
item.chip_hint: A Kopia source of its own: {path} — its folders and its package, with its own retention.
pk.sq_kept_hint: This run couldn't copy the database (failed, too slow, or its disk was asleep) — the last good copy stays in the package, from the run shown.

pk.d_sqlite_text.one: 1 consistent copy of the media server's database (db/sqlite_…) — the server keeps running during the snapshot
pk.d_sqlite_text.other: {n} consistent copies of the media server's databases (db/sqlite_…) — the server keeps running during the snapshot

restore.kopia_items: Apps and VMs with a source of their own: {list} under {root} — inside, every part lies where it lies on the server (<share>/<folder>, and its package).
help.items_text: An app or VM set to «local + offsite» is a Kopia source of its own (.apps/<name> or .vms/<name>) with its own retention. The label says when it last went offsite.
pd.own_sources_hint: — their folders and packages go offsite there, with their own retention; this share leaves them out.
restore.restori: Mr. Restori brings apps and VMs back from them: per app and VM what comes back from where, with dates and ready-made commands.

bubble.waiting.other: {n} new things turned up on the server — I checked three times: they stay only local, and I stop nothing for them, until you decide.

waiting.callout.one: One new thing waits for your decision — only in the local snapshots so far, nothing stops for it:
waiting.callout.other: {n} new things wait for your decision — only in the local snapshots so far, nothing stops for them:

help.waiting_text: What came after the last setup is backed up only locally and not stopped. In appdata and domains, a new folder that belongs to no app or VM, or to a new one, stays in the local snapshots only. If it belongs to an app or VM you set up, it gets that one's level; in other shares it follows its share. A waiting folder brings one notification; «Decide…» opens the setup.
drift_code.new_waiting: New folder {value} — it belongs to no app or VM, or to a new one: only in the local snapshots until you decide (it doesn't go offsite).
drift_code.known_missing: Every new folder of {value} goes offsite. Apply the setup once: then folders that belong to no app or VM, or to a new one, wait for you.
drift_code.new_container: New container {value} — keeps running during the backup until you decide.
drift_code.new_database: New database container {value} — keeps running and gets no dump until you decide (its files are in the snapshot, crash-consistent).
drift_code.new_nextcloud: New Nextcloud container {value} — keeps running, no maintenance mode until you decide.
drift_code.new_vm: New VM {value} — its disks are in the snapshot of their share, but it isn't held for it until you decide.
drift_code.new_vm_unheld: New VM «{name}» — not set up yet; it keeps running until you decide.
drift_code.share_renamed: Share «{old}» is now called «{name}» — «{name}» is only backed up once you've applied the setup.
drift_code.share_new: New share «{name}» ({where}) — not in the setup yet, so not backed up.
drift_code.share_gone_off: Share «{name}» no longer exists — it wasn't backed up anyway.
drift_code.share_gone: Share «{name}» no longer exists, but the setup still backs it up — Apply in «Set up…» takes it out.
drift_code.share_empty: Share «{name}» has no data any more — so far it lay on {locations}.
drift_code.share_deleted_snapshots: Share «{name}» is deleted, but its snapshots ({snapshots}) keep its dataset {datasets}. To let it go: 1. Delete the snapshots on Ms. Snapshotini's page. 2. Delete the share again on the ⟦Shares⟧ tab.
drift_code.share_has_data: Share «{name}» has data now and is backed up — apply the setup once, then I know it again if it's renamed.
drift_code.share_name_bad: Share «{name}»: its name contains @ : " or | — I can't back it up.
drift_code.share_moved: Share «{name}» now lies on {now} (the setup says {was}) — I take it along there by myself.
drift_code.share_live: Share «{name}» can't be backed up with a snapshot — Kopia reads it live, while it's in use.
drift_code.share_snapshot_no_fs: Share «{name}» is set to «local», but it lies on a file system without snapshots — so it has no local backup.
drift_code.share_split: Share «{name}» lies on several disks or pools and has datasets of its own — Kopia sees one subfolder per disk or pool.
drift_code.ct_volumes: Container «{name}» uses Docker volumes ({volumes}) — they live in the Docker image and are NOT in the backup.
drift_code.ct_gone: Container «{name}» is in the setup but no longer exists.
drift_code.vm_off_shared: VM «{name}» is set to «not», but its disks share a dataset — they are in the share's snapshot anyway.
drift_code.vm_whole_device: VM «{name}» uses a whole device as a disk — no snapshot holds it.
drift_code.vm_disk_live: VM «{name}» has a disk on a file system without snapshots — no snapshot holds that disk, and nothing else backs it up.
drift_code.vm_disk_live_kopia: A disk of VM «{name}» has no snapshots. Only the offsite copy of «{share}» has it – read while the VM runs.
drift_code.vm_disk_missing: VM «{name}»: one of its disk files wasn't found.
drift_code.vm_gone: VM «{name}» is in the setup but no longer exists.
drift_code.kopia_no_container: The setup names no Kopia container — nothing goes offsite.
drift_code.kopia_container_gone: The Kopia container «{name}» doesn't exist — nothing goes offsite.
drift_code.kopia_no_mount: The Kopia container doesn't see {path} — map it as {path} → {path} with the access mode ⟦Read Only - Slave⟧.
drift_code.kopia_propagation: The Kopia container sees {path} with the propagation «{propagation}» — new snapshots stay invisible to it. Set the access mode to ⟦Read Only - Slave⟧.
drift_code.kopia_mount_writable: The Kopia container may write into {path} — ⟦Read Only - Slave⟧ is the better access mode.
drift_code.kopia_not_running: The Kopia container «{name}» isn't running — nothing goes offsite.
drift_code.kopia_not_connected: Kopia isn't connected to its repository — nothing goes offsite. Connect it in the KopiaUI.
drift_code.kopia_unreachable: Kopia can't reach its repository, so nothing goes offsite; local backups go on. Check the storage, network, address and key.
drift_code.kopia_uid: Kopia runs as user {uid}, but snapshots need root – so I don't start it. Set PUID=0 and PGID=0 in its template.
drift_code.kopia_identity: Kopia's identity is now {now} (the setup says {was}) — the uploads start new sources instead of carrying on the old ones.
drift_code.kopia_ignores_missing: Kopia's policy for {path} lacks ignore rules ({rules}) — «{name}» isn't given to Kopia until Apply in «Set up…» has set them.
drift_code.kopia_policy_differs: Kopia's policy for {path} differs from the setup — Apply in «Set up…» lines it up again.
drift_code.vm_source_orphan: VM «{name}» has a Kopia source of its own in the setup but no longer exists — what is left of it still goes there.
drift_code.vm_source_off: VM «{name}» is left out of the snapshots but has a Kopia source of its own — only its package goes there.
drift_code.app_source_orphan: App «{name}» has a Kopia source of its own in the setup, but no container of it exists any more — what is left of it still goes there.
drift_code.source_part_unsnapped: Part of «{name}»'s Kopia source, {path}, lies in share «{share}», which takes no snapshot — that part is left out.
drift_code.settings_error: The backup settings (settings.ini) have a mistake: {detail}

setup.new_chip_hint_kopia: New since the last setup. Your default gives it «local + offsite»; the first upload reads it whole. Change its row here, or click to change the default.

setup.new_members_hint: These containers came after the last setup and keep running so far. With Apply they go with this app's choice.

setup.waiting_local_hint: Stays in the local snapshots only; it doesn't go offsite (a rule in this share).
setup.waiting_kopia_hint: Goes offsite from the next backup on, like the other folders of this share. Mind its size: the first upload takes all of it.
setup.waiting_follows_hint: This folder belongs to an app or VM — its choice in step {step} decides.

setup.apply_group_new.one: New on the server — this is how Apply takes it in:
setup.apply_group_new.other: New on the server ({n}) — this is how Apply takes them in:

setup.apply_new_default: Your default for new things ({name}) decided them — change a row before you apply if one should go otherwise.

setup.known_first.other: recorded: {n} folders — a later one gets the level of its app or VM; one of no app or VM, or of a new one, waits for your decision

help.new_text: Whatever came after the last setup is listed first: VMs, apps, shares and folders in appdata or domains that belong to no app or VM, or to a new one. Until you apply, it is backed up only locally; I never send anything offsite or stop it unasked.
help.filter_text: The filter only hides rows; accents in names don't matter. It changes no decision and folds nothing you unfolded. It is empty each time you come. «Decide…» on my main page sets it to «Only what's new» and takes you to the first new thing.
setup.preset.title: The default
setup.preset.sub: What I fill in now — and for whatever turns up later. Afterwards every row is yours to change, and nothing counts before Apply.
setup.preset.auto_new: My own proposals for this server, with a reason on every row. Offsite only where you tick it.
setup.preset.auto_have: Your current settings, plus my proposals for anything new — new things wait for your decision, local only and kept running.
setup.preset.local_text: Every share, app and VM gets local snapshots and its package on this server. Nothing goes offsite.
setup.preset.local_note: Helps against deleting by mistake — not against fire, theft or a dead server.
setup.preset.partner_text: Every share, app and VM gets local snapshots and its package — and every share and VM that is a ZFS dataset of its own goes to the partner office ({partners}) after every backup. Nothing goes to a storage provider.
setup.preset.partner_note: A second copy in another house, readable there (the partner keeps it in plain form); the way there is encrypted. Only ZFS datasets of their own travel.
setup.preset.kopia_partner_tick_wait: counts once you choose this default
setup.preset.kopia_text: Every share, app and VM locally and offsite as well — the full protection, at the price of a big first upload.
setup.preset.kopia_repo: Needs a Kopia container connected to a repository (S3, B2, SFTP …).
setup.preset.kopia_none: There is no Kopia container yet — so this start isn't possible.
setup.preset.kopia_advisor: The Consultant shows how to set one up.

setup.preset.kopia_size.one: Offsite for the first time: {size} in 1 share.
setup.preset.kopia_size.other: Offsite for the first time: {size} in {n} shares.

setup.preset.kopia_vms.one: 1 VM goes along ({list}): Kopia reads its disks whole at the first upload — {size}, though they hold {used}.
setup.preset.kopia_vms.other: {n} VMs go along ({list}): Kopia reads their disks whole at the first upload — {size}, though they hold {used}.

setup.preset.kopia_unknown.one: 1 share whose size I don't know yet: {list}.
setup.preset.kopia_unknown.other: {n} shares whose size I don't know yet: {list}.

setup.preset.kopia_time: At {speed} upload that takes about {time} — the first run uploads that long, and the backups meanwhile are skipped: no new snapshots until it is done.
setup.preset.kopia_time_least: At {speed} upload that takes at least {time} — the first run uploads that long, and the backups meanwhile are skipped: no new snapshots until it is done.
setup.preset.kopia_cost: Your storage provider may charge for that space every month, sometimes for downloading too – check the price before you apply. Films and photos hardly shrink. Or run your own S3 server on a remote Unraid.
setup.preset.media: Media servers keep running during the snapshot.
setup.preset.folders_follow: A new folder in a share that already goes offsite goes along — in {list} it inherits the level of its app or VM; one without an app or VM waits for your decision.
setup.preset.folders_follow_none: A new folder in a share that already goes offsite goes along.
setup.preset.new_later: The default also counts for whatever turns up later. «Automatic» waits for your decision, the other two give their level right away. Apply lists it under «New».
setup.preset.replace: Your current choices in this draft are replaced by the default. What is applied stays as it is until you apply.
setup.preset.replace_new: What you changed in this draft is replaced by this start.
setup.preset.done: Default «{name}» for everything — change any row you like, then apply.
setup.preset.done_new: Default «{name}» for what is new — your settings stay; Apply stores it.
setup.preset.local_new_text: Whatever is new gets local snapshots and its package — a new app is stopped for the snapshot like any other, a new VM held. What goes offsite stays as it is.
setup.preset.kopia_new_text: Whatever is new goes locally and offsite as well — except a new share over 500 GB or of unknown size: that one waits for your decision.
setup.preset.partner_new_text: Whatever is new gets local snapshots and its package — and, where it is a ZFS dataset of its own, goes to the partner office ({partners}) too. What goes offsite stays as it is.
setup.preset.scope_all_hint: Every share, app and VM gets it — what you already chose in this draft is replaced. Anything new that comes later gets it too.
setup.preset.scope_new: Only to what is new — my settings stay
setup.preset.scope_new_hint: What is set up stays as it is. The default applies only to what is new since the last setup, and to whatever comes later.
setup.preset.line_auto: New apps and VMs wait for your decision — only local and kept running until then; a new share isn't backed up at all until then.
setup.preset.kopia_off_new: Offsite is off — new things get local only until you switch it on.
setup.preset.kopia_new_none: Right now nothing new goes offsite for the first time.
help.preset_text: The default fills in the draft: my proposals («Automatic»), «Everything local only» or «Everything local + offsite». «Only to what is new» keeps your settings as they are. «Apply to everything now» gives everything its level and also switches on the backup of your boot device and of the VMs' configuration. Then new things get its level too.
help.never: What I never back up on my own
help.never_text: A default changes nothing here either. The system share, Kopia's own folder, Time Machine targets and VMs that can't be snapshotted stay as they are. Under «local + offsite» a new share over 500 GB, or of unknown size, still waits for you. Media servers keep running during the snapshot. Your Kopia ignore rules stay.
help.partners_text: Then there is a fourth default: «Everything local + partner». It also sends every share and VM that is a ZFS dataset of its own to the partner, after every run. On the card «Everything local + offsite» the tick «also to …» does the same, next to the offsite copy.
setup.known_all: every folder, new ones too — a collection (very many folders at its top)
message.array_stopping: stopped for the array stop — nothing lost, the next run continues
message.settings_missing: the settings are gone — nothing was backed up. Set me up again: «Set up…» → Apply; the backups made so far stay as they are.
bubble.last_array_stop: The last backup {when} stopped when the array was stopped — on purpose: I checked three times, nothing is lost. The next run carries on where the offsite upload was.
notice.array_stop: The last run ({when}) ended because the array was being stopped – on purpose, nothing is lost. The next run backs up as usual and continues the offsite upload.

notice.array_stop_kopia.one: One Kopia source waits for it.

notice.array_stop_left: Held by the array stop: {list}. They come back after the array starts, at the latest with the next run.

stat.kopia_skipped.one: 1 waits for the next run (array stop)
stat.kopia_skipped.other: {n} wait for the next run (array stop)

partner.also_hint: Send it to {name} too: with every backup, after the snapshots, its ZFS snapshot goes there, only the blocks changed since the last one, encrypted on the way
partner.also_on_hint: Goes to {name} too, with every backup after the snapshots — click to leave it out
partner.off_hint: Not backed up — nothing of it can go to a partner
partner.why.not_dataset: Not a dataset of its own (a folder in its pool's dataset) — only a ZFS dataset of its own can go to a partner
partner.why.split: Lies on several pools or disks (or a VM's disks in several datasets) — only one ZFS dataset of its own can go to a partner
partner.why.no_dataset: Not on ZFS, or no dataset of its own — only ZFS datasets go to a partner
partner.why.children: Has datasets inside it that would stay behind — not covered
partner.why.name: Its name can't travel to the partner (only letters, digits, . _ -)
partner.why.not_agreed: The partner runs an older office and takes only what its Team Lead agreed to. His next mutual watch asks for it; after an update there it takes any unit
partner.setup_line: Partners: {names} — the level «local + partner» per VM and share below says what goes there (only ZFS datasets of their own; paired at the Team Lead).
partner.no_key: key missing — pair anew at the Team Lead
partner.place: The backup place (packages, dumps, server/, flash/):
partner.place_hint: The backup place (packages, dumps, server/, flash/) goes to the partner office ({partners}) after every backup too
partner.dep_gap: {app} goes to {partners}, its share {share} doesn't — at the partner its data would be missing.
partner.via_fixed: {share} goes to {partners} as a whole, and this travels inside it — as long as {share} has the partner level. That is decided at the share {share}.
partner.via_vm: Travels with the whole share {share} {where}, its configuration included (XML, UEFI variables, TPM state) — Mr. Restori can start it again from that copy.
partner.via_app: Travels with the whole share {share} {where}, its configuration included (template or compose stack, database dumps) — Mr. Restori can start it again from that copy.
partner.via_decides: Nothing to choose here: the share's level decides.
partner.via_own_source: A level picked here applies to it alone — «local + offsite» then as a Kopia source of its own, with its own retention.
setup.off_in_share: its files still in the snapshot of {share}
setup.off_in_share_hint_vm: Not backed up: the VM is never held, and its configuration is only in the archive of all VMs. Its disks still lie in the snapshot of {share} (at a partner too, when {share} goes to one), caught mid-work. Whether it starts from them is not sure.
setup.off_in_share_hint_app: Not backed up: no stop, no dump, no new package. Its folder still lies in the snapshot of {share} (at a partner too, when {share} goes to one), caught mid-work. A database copied that way may not start.
protection_sum_partner: {kopia} offsite · {partner} local + partner · {snapshot} only local · {off} not backed up
partner.vm_unheld: Its configuration only travels along when the VM is paused or frozen
partner.vm_unheld_hint: If the VM keeps running during the snapshot or isn't backed up, only its disks reach {partners}, without its configuration. It then won't start there from the copy. How to fix it: back it up with «freeze», «pause» or «shut down».
partner.with_place: goes to {partners} with the backup place
partner.with_place_hint: This app binds no folder of its own: its template or compose stack lies in its package in the backup place, and the backup place goes to {partners} after every backup — Mr. Restori there finds it in that copy.
partner.no_folder: No folder of its own: its template or compose stack reaches a partner only when the backup place goes there too (Basics).
prot.partner_hint: Goes to {partners} after every backup, too — the partner office keeps a copy.
partner.own_too: Its folder is a dataset of its own: it goes on its own level, also when {share} goes (a dataset is never part of its share's transfer).

partner.apply_share_off.one: With {share}, 1 app no longer goes to {partner}: {list}.
partner.apply_share_off.other: With {share}, {n} apps no longer go to {partner}: {list}.

partner.apply_keeps: {partner} keeps its copy of {share} until its retention ages it out.
warn_code.partner_old: Partner {partner} runs an older office that can't keep an app on its own — update the office there.
setup.msg.partner_off_app: App {name}: not backed up — nothing of it goes to partner {partner}.

setup.msg.recover_vm_resume: VM {name} is still paused after an aborted run — it stays noted, the next run tries again.
setup.msg.recover_vm_start: VM {name} didn't start again after an aborted run — it stays noted, the next run tries again.
setup.msg.recover_docker_silent: Docker didn't answer — what an aborted run left stopped stays noted, the next run brings it back.
setup.msg.recover_libvirt_silent: The VM service didn't answer — the VMs an aborted run held stay noted, the next run brings them back.
setup.msg.recover_ct_not_ready: Containers started again after an aborted run weren't ready after {seconds} s ({names}) — I went on with the next ones.
setup.msg.recover_nc_gone: Nextcloud {name}, put into maintenance mode by an aborted run, is gone — if its data serves another container now, switch its maintenance mode off by hand.
setup.msg.recover_nc_not_running: Nextcloud {name} isn't running — its maintenance mode stays on after an aborted run; noted, the next run tries again.
setup.msg.recover_nc_no_occ: Nextcloud {name}: its command tool (occ) wasn't found — its maintenance mode stays on after an aborted run; noted, the next run tries again.
setup.msg.recover_back: An aborted run had left things stopped or held — all of it is back: {names}.

partner.choose_text.other: {name} (pair {id}, {address}) is no longer paired at the Team Lead, and several partners here could be it: which one gets its {n} units — {units}? Nothing goes before you choose.

partner.choose_none.other: none of them — the {n} units stay here only

partner.choose_applied.other: The {n} units of {name} go to {to} with this Apply (your choice).

partner.choose_applied_none.other: The {n} units of {name} go to no partner — they stay here only (your choice).

dsw.why: Why not to a partner on its own?
dsw.make: Make it a dataset of its own…
dsw.done: {path} is a dataset of its own now.
dsw.rolled_back: {path}: something went wrong — rolled back, the folder is as it was. Mr. Restori's journal says what.
dsw.failed: {path}: it didn't go through — Mr. Restori's journal says where it stands.
dsw.done_stack: Now start the stack {stack} again in your Compose tool.
partner.uses_other: also uses {folder} — that folder belongs to {owner}

dsw.stack_running: Still running of {stack}: {names} — stop the stack in its Compose tool first.
dsw.no.md_stack_running: Still running of {stack}: {names} — stop the stack in its Compose tool first.
errors.md_stack_running: Still running of {stack}: {names} — stop the stack in its Compose tool first.
dsw.vm: This VM's folder lies in its share's dataset. So it goes to the partner only with the whole share – or as a dataset of its own.
dsw.vm_split: Its disks lie in several datasets — only one dataset of its own can go to a partner. Putting them together is yours to decide.

dsw.share_split: This share lies on several pools or disks — only one dataset can go to a partner. Bringing it onto one pool (the mover) is yours to decide.
dsw.title: Make {name} a dataset of its own
dsw.delicate: A delicate step: {path} is renamed aside, a new ZFS dataset made in its place and everything copied back in. Back the share up first — I keep the old folder until you empty it.
dsw.last_old: The last backup ran {when} — not fresh.
dsw.last_fresh_in: The last backup went well, {when} — {name} is in it.
dsw.last_without: The last backup ran {when} — {name} wasn't in it yet: there is no backup of it.

dsw.stops.one: Stops for it: {list} — started again afterwards.
dsw.stops.other: Stop for it: {list} — started again afterwards.

dsw.stops_none: Nothing that uses it is running — nothing stops.

dsw.no_fresh_ok: I know there is no fresh backup
dsw.started: Started — Mr. Restori's journal shows how {name} goes.
dsw.no.md_not_zfs: {path} doesn't lie on a ZFS pool — only a ZFS folder can become a dataset of its own.
dsw.no.md_split: {path} lies on several pools — bring it onto one first (the mover).
dsw.no.md_already: {path} is a dataset of its own already.

setup.first.point_2: Best on a ZFS pool: snapshots keep earlier backups, and the place may go to a partner office too.
setup.first.point_3: A mirror pool if possible; the array only as a last resort.
setup.first.point_4: One place only: on the pool alone, no secondary storage, no mover.
setup.first.point_5: It stays small (often under a gigabyte) — no big disk needed.

setup.first.offer_pool_mirror: My proposal: only on the pool "{pool}" ({fs}, mirror), no secondary storage.
setup.first.offer_array: My proposal: on the array — there is no pool here.
setup.first.why_same_pool: appdata lies on "{pool}" too, and there is no other ZFS pool. If it fails, apps and backup are gone together — offsite or a partner helps.
setup.first.why_no_zfs_btrfs: There is no ZFS pool here. On "{pool}" (btrfs) snapshots keep earlier backups, but the place can't go to a partner.
setup.first.why_no_zfs: There is no ZFS or btrfs pool here: on "{pool}" only the newest state stays, no earlier ones, and no partner.
setup.first.why_no_pool: The array is only a last resort: the share spreads over several disks, there's no snapshot of the whole and no partner.
setup.first.asleep: The pool "{pool}" is asleep, and I don't wake it. Wake it on the ⟦Main⟧ page, then it works.
setup.first.asleep_array: A disk of the array is asleep, and I don't wake it. Wake it on the ⟦Main⟧ page, then it works.
setup.first.known: Unraid knew the share {share} already — it may come back with a disk or a folder. So I don't create it anew: have a look under ⟦Shares⟧, or take another one.
setup.first.own_title: Rather create it in Unraid yourself
setup.first.own_text: Under ⟦Shares⟧ with "⟦Add Share⟧" — name suggestion {name}, on a ZFS pool and only there (no secondary storage).
setup.first.pick_hint: Only shares that fit (not appdata, system, domains, isos). What speaks against one I say right after, under «Basics» — you can change it there any time.
setup.first.confirm_text: Unraid creates the share with its own "⟦Add Share⟧", as on the ⟦Shares⟧ page:
setup.first.c_exclusive_no: ⟦No⟧ — Unraid doesn't permit exclusive shares right now (⟦Global Share Settings⟧); it still lies on this pool only
setup.first.c_export_no: ⟦No⟧ — Unraid's default for a new share: the packages stay off the network
setup.first.confirm_after: Then I look at the server again and take it as the backup place — you can change that under «Basics».
errors.place_exists: The share {share} is there already — choose it as the backup place.
errors.place_known: Unraid knew the share {share} already — I don't create it anew. Have a look under ⟦Shares⟧.
errors.place_pool_unknown: Unraid doesn't know the pool "{pool}" — have another look at my proposal.
errors.place_pool_asleep: The pool "{pool}" is asleep, and I don't wake it. Wake it on the ⟦Main⟧ page and try again.
errors.place_array_asleep: A disk of the array is asleep, and I don't wake it. Wake it on the ⟦Main⟧ page and try again.
tile.place_first: The backup place first — under «Set up»
fit.docker_off: Mr. Backupsy would come — but whether Kopia is here for the offsite copy he can't tell: Docker isn't running.
waiting.apps_unknown: new apps: not looked for — Docker isn't running

waiting.callout_unsure.one: One new thing waits for your decision — nothing stops for it, and whether a snapshot holds it isn't known yet:
waiting.callout_unsure.other: {n} new things wait for your decision — nothing stops for them, and not every one is known to be in a local snapshot:

bubble.waiting_unsure.one: Something new turned up – I checked three times! I stop nothing for it until you decide. The setup shows whether a snapshot has it.
bubble.waiting_unsure.other: {n} new things turned up – I checked three times! I stop nothing for them until you decide. Not every one is surely in a snapshot yet.

vm.not_set_up_unknown: Mr. Backupsy doesn't know yet how to treat it. Whether a snapshot holds it, «Set up…» → VMs shows. It keeps running meanwhile.
vm.not_set_up_none: Not backed up: no snapshot holds its disks, and Mr. Backupsy doesn't know how to treat it. How to fix it: «Set up…» → VMs.
mode_hint.nodocker: Docker isn't running: only snapshots of the shares and VMs, and the flash. No dumps, no app packages, nothing offsite.
mode_hint.nodocker_partners: Docker isn't running: only snapshots of the shares and VMs, the flash and the partners' copies ({partners}). No dumps, no app packages, nothing offsite.
mode_hint.docker_silent: Docker is switched on but doesn't answer: the backup would end at once, before it stops or saves anything. Restart Docker under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Docker⟧ first.
mode_hint.backup_held: Dumps and local snapshots, nothing goes offsite: the offsite copy is held until you have looked at it (above). Containers stop for a few minutes.
mode_hint.backup_stuck: Dumps, snapshots and the offsite upload – but the storage there has taken nothing since {when}, so the upload fails. Containers stop for a few minutes.
stat.missed: the scheduled backup of {when} didn't run

stat.db_old.other: {n} kept from earlier backups, the oldest {when}

bubble.warn_in_log: Which warning it was, its log says — click the backup under «Last runs».
setup.level_hint.vm_0: Not backed up: never held for the snapshot, no package of its own, nothing goes offsite.
setup.level_hint.vm_1: Local snapshot of its disks, held for it as chosen on its row; its package (XML, UEFI variables, TPM state) goes to the backup place.
setup.app_nodata_off: This app binds no folder in a share, and at «off» it gets no package: its template or compose file lies on the flash and goes with its backup.
setup.off_in_share_hint_vm_nolibvirt: Not backed up: the VM is never held, and without the VM archive its configuration is missing. Its disks still lie in the snapshot of {share} (at a partner too, when {share} goes to one), caught mid-work. Whether it starts is not sure.
setup.asleep.chip_place: {names} is asleep right now. The backup place lies there too, so every backup wakes it anyway — the packages are the point.
setup.sources.row_other_manual: {what}: not the office's — this Apply sets it to «manual» too (untick below to leave it as it is)

setup.apply_sources_manual.one: Kopia: 1 old source is set to «manual» — Kopia no longer schedules it, its snapshots stay: {list}
setup.apply_sources_manual.other: Kopia: {n} old sources are set to «manual» — Kopia no longer schedules them, their snapshots stay: {list}
